title: RVLRY: review the phone UX mockups
summary: Eight screen proposals covering thumb reach, visible words, team/round progress, handoffs and resume/new-game choices. Choose a direction and leave feedback here.
body:
# RVLRY phone UX review

The Pixel test succeeded across closes and force-closes. APK-over-APK updating remains untested. These are UX proposals; the installed APK is unchanged.

## Visual mockups
Open **JNAS → Media → DropBox → RVLRY-phone-flow-proposal.html** in a browser.

Windows path: `\\JNAS\Media\DropBox\RVLRY-phone-flow-proposal.html`

Kestrel strips the CSS and scripts used by the storyboard. This is its companion review; the original HTML contains the actual visual mockups. Names, words and scores are illustrative. It demonstrates selected interactions, not a complete game.

## Recommended progress indicator
Use two levels: round segments for the whole game, and labeled team cells for the current round. Text and borders carry meaning as well as color. The tracker is informational, never a way to jump turns.

**Round 2 of 3 · Team 2 of 3**

| Foxes | Otters | Owls |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Complete | NOW · Maya presents | NEXT · Leo presents |

Each team gets one turn per round. Its presenter rotates on its next turn. Setup uses Settings → Teams → Review instead.

The alternative whole-game grid shows every team in every round, but uses more space. I recommend the compact strip, with the grid available on demand if useful.

## Eight screen proposals

| Screen | What should be obvious | Main action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Saved game | Paused game, team, round and remaining time | Resume, with Start new game also visible |
| Setup | Team being edited; first presenter and next presenter | Continue to next team, then review |
| Handoff | Maya presents for Otters; Sam guesses; Leo follows | I'm Maya — ready, then Start my turn |
| Playing | Current clue first; time and current team easy to find | Large bottom Skip and Correct |
| Turn recap | Maya finished; Otters scored 5; all words visible | Pass phone to Leo |
| Round complete | All teams finished; scores and next presenter | Pass phone to Alex for Round 3 |
| Paused | Clock stopped; clue hidden; return phone to presenter | Resume, Save and leave, or Start new game |
| Final results | All turns complete; winner and standings | Play again with these teams or Back to games |

### Playing: hierarchy and thumb reach
The clue has the strongest emphasis. Three recent correct/skipped words remain visible; skipped rows can be tapped to retry. Skip and Correct are 76 pixels high in the mockup and separated by a gap. Pause sits below; ending a turn early should live in the pause options.

Implementation must preserve access to older skipped words and optional hints, and check long names, four teams, larger text and keyboard layouts.

### Recap and handoff
Keep the finished team's identity through its full word recap even if the engine has already advanced. Then explicitly pass the phone. Mark round boundaries and name the next presenter. After the final turn, show results with no next-team prompt.

### Resume versus new game
Offer both immediately, without requiring a resume first. Confirm before replacing a save; allow retaining teams/settings. Cancelling preserves the current game.

### Visual treatment
Retain the warm background and teal identity. Strengthen borders and current-team emphasis; distinguish completed turns and amber skipped-word controls. Meaning must not depend on color alone.

## Your feedback
Start with Playing, Handoff and Turn recap in the HTML. Answer below and add screen-specific notes. Your next-step choice records the scope you want when work resumes; submitting does not launch an agent automatically.

This review covers Who What Where. Hat Game and Imposter need their own role/privacy and phase reviews before adapting these patterns.

questions.label: Which progress indicator should we develop?
options: Compact round segments plus current-round team strip
Whole-game grid visible on gameplay screens
Compact strip with whole-game grid available on demand (recommended)
Rework the indicator; see my notes

questions.label: What word visibility do you want during a turn? The full recap would remain afterward.
options: Three recent words, with access to all skipped words
More recent words visible, even if the list scrolls
Prioritize outstanding skipped words over correct-word history
Mostly improve the end-of-turn recap; keep play simpler

questions.label: How should starting a turn work after passing the phone?
options: Confirm I am the presenter, then tap Start turn
One explicit Start turn button naming the presenter
Unsure; refine the handoff before deciding

questions.label: What would you change about controls, thumb reach, hierarchy, grouping, colors or current/next participant clarity? Mention screen names where useful.
What should happen when we resume this work?
options: Implement the proposed Who What Where UX, incorporating my answers
Revise the mockups using my feedback before implementation
Discuss my feedback with me first

questions.label: Anything else, including resume/new-game options or the exact round and team flow?
